newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Seven bodies found in Malaysia helicopter crash.
newsitem.headline: Seven bodies found in Malaysia helicopter crash.

text.p: Rescue workers pulled out seven bodies from the wreckage of two Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) helicopters on Thursday and said they were looking for four more missing people.
"We have seven confirmed dead and are looking for another four," RMAF spokesman Ramli Abdul Rahim told Reuters.
Some 102 workers from the police and army were involved in the search, he said.

The two Nuri helicopters, carrying 11 military personnel, crashed in a hilly region of the east Malaysian state of Sabah on Borneo island on Tuesday while returning from a routine mission in the remote district of Long Pasia in Sabah.
The Defence Ministry did not say how the two helicopters crashed. Ramli said the air force had begun an inquiry.
Local newspapers speculated the two helicopters could have collided.
The helicopters were scheduled to arrive at their base on Labuan island off Borneo at 4.55 p.m. (0900 GMT) on Tuesday. RMAF said last radio contact with the aircraft was at 4.21 p.m.

The latest incident brings to 14 the number of U.S.-made Nuri helicopters that have crashed since their purchase in 1968. Before Tuesday's incident, the previous crashes involving Nuri helicopters had claimed 60 lives.
In October last year, a Nuri helicopter crashed at sea while airlifting an injured Thai sailor to hospital. Three crew members were killed in the incident.
All Nuri helicopters were grounded for nearly a month after the crash and were only allowed to resume flights after the air force was satisfied with their safety.
